summary: Honoré-Joseph Chavée was a scholar of linguistics and Indology. He studied at KU Leuven under Félix Nève (~1841–1844) and under Eugène Burnouf (~1845–1848). He held posts at the Royal Military Academy, Collège Stanislas, Scuola Normale Superiore di Pisa, and École Supérieure de Guerre.

Honsho Ueda is a scholar in Buddhist studies. He served as a lecturer (attested 1963) and professor (attested 1992) at Minobusan Junior College, professor at Minobusan University (attested 1996), and director at the Institute for Advanced Studies on Asia (attested 1996).
Hoong Teik Toh works in Sinology, Tibetology, and Buddhist studies. He earned a PhD from Harvard University in 2004, having studied under Gray Tuttle, Ruohong Li, and Yudru Tsomu.

Horace Arthur Rose worked in Indology and history and archaeology. He was educated at St Paul's School and Emmanuel College (~1886–1889) and served as a civil servant in the Indian Civil Service from 1888 to 1917.

Horace Geoffrey Quaritch Wales studied Indology and history and archaeology. Educated at Queens' College and SOAS under Charles Otto Blagden (PhD 1931), he worked at King's College, Bangkok, the Greater India Society (~1934–1941), and the Royal Asiatic Society (1964–1968).

Horace Hayman Wilson was an Indologist who studied under Henry Thomas Colebrooke. He served at the Kolkata Mint (1816–1833), held the Boden Chair of Sanscrit at Oxford (1831–1860), and was Director of the Royal Asiatic Society (1837–1860).

Horace Irvin Poleman was an Indologist who studied at the University of Pennsylvania under W. Norman Brown. He held posts at Penn, Yale, the U.S. Embassy in New Delhi, and headed the Oriental Division at the Library of Congress (1955–1965).

Horace L. Friess was a religious studies and philosophy scholar who studied at Columbia University (~1915–1918) and Heidelberg University. He held posts at Johns Hopkins University and Columbia University, where he became Joseph L. Buttenwieser Professor of Human Relations (1962–1966).
Horkhang Sonam Palbar was a Tibetology scholar. He studied under Tsadru Ngawang Losang and Gendun Chophel (~1946–1951).
Horst Brinkhaus is an Indologist. He held posts at the University of Münster (attested 1978) and Kiel University (~1994–2010).
Horst Fichtner was a scholar in Indology and history and archaeology. He earned a Dr. med. from the University of Leipzig in 1924 and taught social ethics at Humboldt University of Berlin in 1945.

Horst Lasic is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He completed a PhD at the University of Vienna in 1999 and held posts at the Austrian Academy of Sciences (1995) and the University of Vienna (1999).

Hosakote Krishna Sastri worked in Indology and history and archaeology. He served at the Archaeological Survey of India as Assistant Superintendent for Epigraphy (~1904–1920) and Government Epigraphist for India (~1920–1925), a post he also held for the Government of India.
Hoseok Leigh works in philosophy and religious studies. He studied under Ha-u Kim and Cheonghwa, and earned a PhD from the California Institute of Integral Studies (attested 2010).
Hoseong Kim is a scholar in philosophy, Indology, and Buddhist studies. He founded the Nihon Bukkyōshi Kenkyūjo (attested 2011) and served as a professor at Dongguk University (attested 2011).
Hoshu Mitsuhara was a Buddhist studies scholar who served at Koyasan University as a professor (attested 1982) and later as professor emeritus (attested 2004).

Hotetsu Matsumoto works in Buddhist studies, Indology, and Tibetology. He held a post at Tohoku University (attested 1997) and serves as a professor and director of the Clinical Esoteric Buddhism Center at Shuchiin University (attested 2026).

Hoyo Watanabe was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Rissho University (~1952–1956). He spent his career there as a faculty professor (~1973–2004), dean of Buddhist studies (attested 1984–1985), and special honorary professor (~2004–2021).
Hozen Seki was a Buddhist studies figure who founded the American Buddhist Academy and served as resident minister at the New York Buddhist Church (attested 1998).

Hrachia Adjarian was a scholar of linguistics and Iranian/Central Asian studies. He studied at the University of Strasbourg under Heinrich Hübschmann and under Antoine Meillet, holding posts at the Aramiyan School (1893), Sanasarian College (1894), and Yerevan State University (1923).
